text: Two balls A and B are placed at the top of 180 m tall tower. Ball A is released from the top at t = 0 s. Ball B is thrown vertically down with an initial velocity 'u' at t = 2 s. After a certain time, both balls meet 100 m above the ground. Find the value of 'u' in $ms^{-1}$. [use $g = 10 ms^{-2}$] :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As the meeting point lies $100\mathrm{m}$ above ground, displacement of ball will be $80\mathrm{m}$.

For ball $A$

$\begin{array}{l} u=0,\mathrm{S}=80\mathrm{m},a=+\mathrm{g}=+10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\text{, time}=t_{1} \\  \\ \Rightarrow S=ut+\dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 80=0+\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times t_{1}{}^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{160}{10}=t_{1}{}^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow t_{1}=4\mathrm{s} \end{array}$

As ball $B$ is thrown after 2 seconds after release of $A$. Thus, time available for ball $B$ is 2 seconds to cover a distance of $80\mathrm{m}$.

Let speed be ' $u$ ' $\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s},t_{2}=4-2=2\mathrm{s},\mathrm{S}=80\mathrm{m}$, $a=+g=+10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

$\therefore 80=u\times 2+\frac{1}{2}\times 10\times (2)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 80=2u+20$

$\Rightarrow 2u=60$

$\Rightarrow u=30\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift

text: A body of mass M at rest explodes into three pieces, in the ratio of masses 1 : 1 : 2. Two smaller pieces fly off perpendicular to each other with velocities of $30 ms^{-1}$ and $40 ms^{-1}$ respectively. The velocity of the third piece will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given problem a body of mass $M$ explodes into three pieces of mass ratio $1:1:2$

$\therefore$ Mass of fragments will be $x,x,2x$ 

Hence, $M=x+x+2x=4x\mathrm{kg}$

As in the process of explosion no external forces are involved and explosion occurs due to internal forces. Thus, momentum of the system will be conserved.

$p_{\text{initial}}=p_{\text{final}}$

By law of conservation of momentum,

$M\times 0=\frac{M}{4}\times 30\hat{i}+\frac{M}{4}\times 40\hat{j}+\frac{2M}{4}⃗{v}$

Where $⃗{v}$ is the velocity of the third fragment.

$\frac{M⃗{v}}{2}=-\frac{M}{4}(30\hat{i}+40\hat{j})$

$\Rightarrow$ $⃗{v}=-15\hat{i}-20\hat{j}$

Thus, magnitude of $⃗{v}=|⃗{v}|=\sqrt{v_{x}^{2}+v_{y}^{2}}$ $=\sqrt{(-15)^{2}+(-20)^{2}}$

$|⃗{v}|=\sqrt{625}=25\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift

text:
A spherical shell of 1 kg mass and radius R is rolling with angular speed $ω$ on horizontal plane (as shown in figure). The magnitude of angular momentum of the shell about the origin O is $\frac{a}{3}$ $R^{2}ω$. The value of a will be :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Rolling without slipping gives $v_{cm}=ωR$; the centre is at height $R$ above the $x$-axis through O and moves along $+x$.

Angular momentum about O is the angular momentum of the centre of mass about O plus the spin about the centre:

$L_{O}=mv_{cm}R+I_{cm}ω$

The centre moves along $+x$ at height $R$ and the shell spins clockwise, so both terms point into the page and add. For a thin spherical shell $I_{cm}=\dfrac{2}{3}mR^{2}$:

$L_{O}=m(ωR)R+\dfrac{2}{3}mR^{2}ω=\dfrac{5}{3}mR^{2}ω$

With $m=1\text{kg}$, $L_{O}=\dfrac{5}{3}R^{2}ω$, so $a=5$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift

text: Two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ have equal magnitudes. If magnitude of $\vec{A}$ + $\vec{B}$ is equal to two times the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ $-$ $\vec{B}$, then the angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sqrt{A^{2}+A^{2}+2A^{2}\cos θ}=2\sqrt{A^{2}+A^{2}+2A^{2}(-\cos θ)}$

$\Rightarrow 2A^{2}+2A^{2}\cos θ=8A^{2}-8A^{2}\cos θ$

$\Rightarrow 5\cos θ=3$

$\Rightarrow θ=\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{3}{5}\right )$

text: A parallel beam of light is allowed to fall on a transparent spherical globe of diameter 30 cm and refractive index 1.5. The distance from the centre of the globe at which the beam of light can converge is $_____________ mm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


1st refraction : $\frac{1.5}{v_{1}}-0=\frac{0.5}{15}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1} = 45 cm$

2nd refraction : $\frac{1}{v_{2}}-\frac{1.5}{15}=\frac{-0.5}{-15}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{v_{2}}=\frac{1}{30}+\frac{1}{10}$

$=\frac{4}{30}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2} = + 7.5 cm$

$\Rightarrow$ Distance from centre = 22.5 cm = 225 mm
